formalDefinition: TOPOLOGICALSORT = {<G> | G is a DAG with a valid linear ordering of vertices such that for every directed edge (u,v), u appears before v}
problemDefinition: Topological Sort is the problem of arranging the vertices of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) into a linear sequence such that all directed edges point forward in the sequence. If the graph contains a cycle, no valid topological ordering exists.
outputDescription: A valid topological ordering of the vertices of G
source: Kahn, A. B. (1962). Topological sorting of large networks. Communications of the ACM, 5(11), 558-562.
certificateFormat: Format: (q0,...,qn) | linear ordering of all nodes, each qi appears once, u before v for every (u,v) in E Example: (1,2,3,4,5,6)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: Kahn's algorithm is a BFS-based approach to topological sorting. It repeatedly removes vertices with zero in-degree from the graph, appending them to the output ordering. If all vertices are removed, the ordering is valid; otherwise, the graph contains a cycle and no topological sort exists.
defaultSolver.source: Kahn, A. B. (1962). Topological sorting of large networks. Communications of the ACM, 5(11), 558-562.

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: Given a proposed ordering of vertices, the verifier checks that (1) every vertex in the graph appears exactly once in the ordering, and (2) for every directed edge (u,v) in the graph, u appears before v in the ordering.
defaultVerifier.source: Kahn, A. B. (1962). Topological sorting of large networks. Communications of the ACM, 5(11), 558-562.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Animates the graph by topological rank: all source nodes (in-degree zero) highlight first, followed by their successors in waves. This mirrors how Kahn's Algorithm peels off layers of zero-in-degree nodes during execution. Every edge is highlighted because, in a valid topological ordering, every directed edge points forward.
defaultVisualization.source: Kahn, A. B. (1962). Topological sorting of large networks. Communications of the ACM, 5(11), 558-562.
